u02-rem-close.resolution: Checked clause by clause against the locked Greek after the a20 corrections. (1) Psalm 33:8 [34:7] is correct (the lane itself concludes 'no defect'). (2) βαλὼν λίθον 'laid a cornerstone' is the standard rendering of the Job 38:6 idiom. The ὅτι οὕτως ἕστηκεν clause and the ὡσπερεὶ comparison are idiomatic English. 'Who for our sake became flesh' is a normal rendering of an attributive participle. Psalm 117:22 [118:22] is the identification of κατὰ τὸ ἐν ψαλμοῖς per the house citation convention. ἀμέλει, ὁ δὲ and μὲν/δὲ are particles, and 'He' as the subject of κατέχει (God) is clear from context. (3) The eagle/vulture lemma (Ἐπὶ δὲ σῷ προστάγματι ὑψοῦται ἀετός … ἐπ' ἐξοχῇ πέτρας καὶ ἀποκρύφῳ) is present in this section's Greek, and Job 38:41 is correct. (4) Job references follow the edition's own chapter/verse markers (Κεφ. ΛΘ, κζʹ; λδʹ; Κεφ. Μʹ, βʹ), which are the LXX numbering used throughout this work. 'He yielded the first place' keeps the Greek's unexpressed subject. (5) ἀφίασιν 'give them free rein' (let them go at it), 'I care' for μέλει μοι, and 'freedom to speak' for παρρησία are acceptable idiom. χρηματισμός/κεχρηματικέναι rendered 'dealing/dealt with' follows the standard LXX English (Brenton, Job 40:3) and is applied consistently to both of the commentator's senses. No meaning error.

(4) 'I have lost my case before You' for Ἥττημαι παρὰ σοὶ τὸ δικαίωμα is a fair idiomatic rendering of being defeated in one's plea. (5) Rendering ὅτι recitativum and indirect speech as direct quotation is a standard English choice that keeps the meaning (God's self-defense, the purpose 'to show you righteous', and the paraphrase προτεταχέναι με … 'I arranged beforehand'). No meaning error.
